question.text: What is the purpose of a Power of Attorney (POA) in the context of retirement planning?

answer.text: To distribute assets after death according to the grantor's wishes
To authorize another person to make financial and legal decisions on behalf of the grantor
To specify medical treatment preferences in case of incapacitation
To nominate beneficiaries for insurance policies

explanation.text: The Logic: As per the workbook, a Power of Attorney authorizes another person to act on behalf of the grantor and conduct transactions when the grantor is unable to do so themselves. The Trap: Option A describes a Will; Option C describes an Advance Medical Directive; Option D describes nomination under an insurance policy. None of these is a POA. Note: POA is about delegation of authority on behalf of the grantor; the workbook page does not differentiate between durable and regular POA in terms of validity on incapacity.
